key_insight: Long-range circuit noise fragility depends on fault-phase interference with the target Hamiltonian, not simply on how widely faults spread.
engineering_relevance: Noise-aware ansatz design should control transverse catalysts and balance coherent expressivity against gate-count exposure λ = pK.
method: Prove contrasting energy damage for equally extensive faults in Heisenberg chains.
Test catalyst suppression and annealing during noisy variational training with long-range ZZ gates.
Combine single-fault fragility with gate-count exposure to predict noise-induced energy shifts.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact N/2 damage ratio between equal-support faults; suppressing both catalyst types eliminates the fragility plateau and halves dephasing error.
watch_item: The reported guarantees concern Heisenberg chains and the studied circuit and noise settings; broader hardware applicability requires validation.
paper_title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
